text:
ashley: Hey team — hitting 403 in the console when I accept a guest invite and try to switch to the project. Works for the owner but guests see no actions (buttons grayed). Anyone else?

matt: I saw a couple of reports earlier today. Can you paste the user and org id? also which identity provider (Okta/GSuite)?

ashley: org: org-7kpq, project: proj-83h, user email: ashley+guest@acme.com, using Okta SSO. Invite accepted successfully but console shows "You do not have permission" and all buttons disabled.

kevin: Two quick checks — is the invite a guest/cross-tenant link? sometimes SCIM group claims don't map for external guests and you end up with no project role.

ashley: It's a guest invite (external collaborator). The invite flow said "Guest (external)".

sara_support: Thanks, Ashley. Filing an initial support ticket and assigning to infra for role-propagation check. Can you try repro steps for us and include a HAR or console logs? Also, does the API work for this user (e.g., can they call the /v1/projects endpoint)?

ashley: API call returns 403 too: 

```
GET https://api.redwood.example/v1/projects/proj-83h
Authorization: Bearer <token-from-browser>
=> 403 {"error":"forbidden","message":"insufficient_scope"}
```

matt: That looks like a token-scope mapping issue during SSO exchange. Okta sometimes strips the "roles" claim for guests. Can you check the id_token claims in the browser network tab?

ashley: Pasted the id_token payload (decoded): 

```
{
  "sub": "00u1a...",
  "email": "ashley+guest@acme.com",
  "groups": [],
  "roles": null,
  "iss": "https://acme.okta.com"
}
```

kevin: groups empty and roles null — that's the problem. Our role-mapper treats null as no bindings which leads to effective deny on console. Two paths: 1) workaround - grant explicit project-level collaborator role to the user in the org admin UI, 2) fix upstream SCIM/claim mapping for guest accounts.

ashley: Is there a quick workaround? customer is blocked from reviewing data.

jenna: I can apply a manual role binding for the user — need approval from the org owner. @ashley who is owner on org-7kpq?

ashley: owner is tom@acme.com. I can ping him.

infra-bot: Ticket #SUP-1129 created and linked to infra-pipeline. Assigning to kevin. ETA triage: 1h.

kevin: For triage notes: looks like SCIM group sync ignored external collaborator groups because of the 'external_user' flag in Okta SCIM payload. When that happens our claim sanitizer strips groups to avoid leaking internal roles. This behavior is intentional but needs an override for invited guests when org admin expects project-level access.

matt: Proposed immediate fix: add a service-side fallback that checks "pending_invite" or "accepted_invite" records during SSO login and rehydrate the role mapping from the invite metadata. That avoids waiting on IdP changes. I'll draft a tiny patch.

sara_support: For the customer right now, manual role binding is fastest. After that, we can roll a fix and flip the flag.

ashley: Tom approved. Jenna, please add "Project Collaborator" to ashley+guest@acme.com for proj-83h.

jenna: Done. Confirmed via admin UI and db: 

```
INSERT INTO role_bindings (org_id, project_id, principal, role) VALUES ('org-7kpq','proj-83h','user:ashley+guest@acme.com','project:collaborator');
```

ashley: Buttons now active, can perform actions. Thanks! :tada:

kevin: Pushed a small PR to rehydrate invite roles on SSO login: will add tests for guest flow. If CI passes I'll schedule a canary deploy to staging.

infra-bot: SUP-1129 updated: patch landed in staging, canary deploy scheduled.

matt: Postmortem action items: 1) document guest invite claim behavior in support KB, 2) add a telemetry alert for when users decode tokens with null roles but have accepted_invite records, 3) patch rollout plan.

ashley: Great — please keep me posted. Also adding a one-line KB we can send to the customer for root cause.

sara_support: Closing the immediate customer-facing loop: manual binding applied and customer recovered. Keeping ticket open for engineering fix.

jenna: Customer follow-up message sent: "Your access is restored; we are rolling a permanent fix to ensure guest invites map roles correctly on SSO logins."

ashley: Thanks all! :heart:
